entities.summary: The post-imperial period was the final stage of ancient Assyrian history, covering the history of the Assyrian heartland from the fall of the Neo-Assyrian Empire in 609 BC to the final sack and destruction of Assur, Assyria's ancient religious capital, by the Sasanian Empire c. AD 240. There was no independent Assyrian state during this time, with Assur and other Assyrian cities instead falling under the control of the successive Median, Neo-Babylonian, Achaemenid, Seleucid and Parthian empires. The period was marked by the continuance of ancient Assyrian culture, traditions and religion, despite the lack of an Assyrian kingdom.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The post-imperial Assyria played a significant role in preserving ancient Assyrian culture and traditions despite the lack of an independent Assyrian state. The period saw the continuation of Assyrian religious practices and the transmission of classical Assyrian knowledge to subsequent empires.
